witnesses.provenance: Solana's per-transaction MAX_COMPUTE_UNIT_LIMIT is 1,400,000 compute units. It is the chain's limit, not ours. The campaign sets ProgramTest's ceiling to exactly that value and never raises it.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.wire_bytes > 1232) | select((.label | test("Issue|issue|Unwrap|unwrap|K_i skew|receipt backed|cross-schema|recipe substitution")) | not)] | length | tostring
witnesses.provenance: Solana's legacy packet maximum is 1,232 bytes (PACKET_DATA_BYTES). This campaign used to assert that its largest frame fit; at the K = 3 campaign basis it does NOT, and the honest witness is which frames are over rather than a claim that none are. Every transaction past the limit is one of the two FULL-WIDTH structured actions or a hostile shaped like one: RepresentationRequestV2::validate refuses IssueStructured/UnwrapStructured unless asset_count == outcome_count (request.rs:470-481), so those two carry K asset rows and K materialized account quadruples while every selected-outcome action carries exactly one. A frame over the limit that is NOT one of those would mean the wall moved somewhere nobody measured.

THE MEASUREMENT. A v0 message carrying IssueStructured or UnwrapStructured at K = 3, compiled against a real activated Address Lookup Table, is 1,357 bytes against a 1,232-byte limit -- over by 125. The ALT is not an unpulled lever here: it is what takes the same frame from 2,594 down to 1,357, so the house v0/ALT pattern is applied and the frame is still too wide. Decision 0011 s3b measured the executable ceiling at K = 3 from the RequestProfile artifact (29 + 8K operations at 24 bytes against REQUEST_PROFILE_MAX_BYTES_V1 = 1312) and called it hard; the packet caps the two full-width actions at K = 2, one coordinate lower, and nothing had measured it because this route had never been submitted at K = 3. A coordinate costs ASSET_BYTES_V2 + 2 * RATIONAL_ASSET_ACCOUNT_COUNT_V2 = 168 wire bytes; the campaign derives the ceiling from that constant and two measurements in the_full_width_structured_frame_does_not_fit_a_packet_at_k_three.

The selected-outcome actions -- Denominate, Reconstitute, RedeemTerminal -- carry asset_count == 1 at every K, so their request is 488 + 160 bytes at any representation width and their frames fit with room. So a K = 3 Structured product can be denominated, reconstituted and redeemed on a cluster and can never be issued or unwrapped there; this witness is the half of that sentence the previous packet witness used to cover for the whole campaign.
A `wire_bytes` of null says the campaign did not measure, which is honest but is not a claim that the frame fits. This asserts that no transaction in this campaign is unmeasured.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.error != null) | select([.logs[] | select(contains("custom program error: 0x"))] | length == 0)] | length | tostring
witnesses.provenance: The Solana runtime reports a privilege, frame, or account refusal it decides ITSELF as a bare InstructionError with no `custom program error:` log line; that line appears only when a program returned ProgramError::Custom. Every refusal this campaign claims -- named or unnamed_refusal -- is a program decision, so a bare runtime refusal appearing here would mean a hostile case stopped being about a program.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.label | endswith("commits")) | .logs[] | select(. == "Program TokenzQdBNbLqP5VEhdkAS6EPFLC1PHnBqCXEpPxuEb success")] | length | tostring
witnesses.provenance: This campaign's Token-2022 fixture is the byte-for-byte canonical, cross-host-reproducible spl-token-2022 11.0.0 ELF pinned in programs/dclutch-claims-sbf/fixtures/token-2022-v11.provenance (SHA-256 e2acdfb750881462ad613a15cc9c54ae17ce066580e867e1e635fbdfe01f5697), authenticated at TokenzQdBNbLqP5VEhdkAS6EPFLC1PHnBqCXEpPxuEb -- Solana's real, deployed Token-2022 program address, which only the canonical artifact can occupy under the fixture's own digest check. This counts the runtime's own success logs for it across the six committing transactions, and the count is a function of the campaign basis width K: IssueStructured 4 (K = 3 shard transfers plus the receipt mint), UnwrapStructured 4 (the receipt burn plus K shard transfers), Denominate 1, Reconstitute 1, winning terminal 2, losing terminal 1 -- thirteen. It was eleven at K = 2 and it moves with K by design, so a silent width change fails here.

witnesses.query: .transactions[] | select(.label == "claims rational-representation-v2: caller refuses after a complete terminal redemption") | (if .error == null then "committed" else ([.logs[] | select(. == "Program GCkWCknJ46pyPNHC9DPjTxedvjLHYJUVioxe7X5o6xa4 success")] | length | tostring) end)
witnesses.provenance: A rollback case is only evidence if the thing being rolled back actually happened. This asserts, from the runtime's own log, that a transaction the ledger records as FAILED contains a completed Claims invocation (which itself only returns after real Custody and real Token-2022 both succeeded, per the terminal redemption's own account frame). The `if .error == null` guard makes a campaign that accidentally let the transaction commit fail this witness rather than pass it.

The budgets live in tools/gauntlet/CU_BUDGETS.json; this witness carries no number of its own. The independent value is Solana's 1,400,000 per-transaction MAX_COMPUTE_UNIT_LIMIT. This campaign carried no CU witness at all until the wallet payout landed, which is why its three rows are the only ones named: they are the first routes a WALLET reaches on its own, so a regression here is a regression a user meets rather than one a keeper absorbs. Every transaction a budget row names is a LITERAL label the recorder emits; the wildcards in bindings.json are the census's and must never be copied into a budget, which would make the row AMBIGUOUS.
